name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea rose to $535 a tonne after gas cuts to plants; Hormuz flows near pre-war levels but tanker attacks go on
state: Egyptian granular urea rose to $535 a tonne FOB in November, about 17% above September's $457, after gas deliveries to nitrogen plants were cut by up to 20% from 1 Nov (UkrAgroConsult, 10 Nov). Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, though attacks on tankers continued at about one a day in November (The Edge Malaysia, 20 Nov). That is short of a 60% three-month rise, several exporters restricting at once or a closed route, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher prices from some suppliers, which can feed into crop costs and food prices later in 2027.
rubric_hit: Egypt gas cuts curbing a major exporter's output = Watch; urea +17% since Sep, below +60% Alert line

sources.title: UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions
The Edge Malaysia — Oil prices set for third straight weekly decline on Middle East export flows

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
